item.title: Always log your entire configuration when booting
item.description: Here is a small tip that has saved me a lot of time: Always log your entire parsed configuration when your service or application boots. Or at least, support logging it through a verbose logging level. In practice, this can be logging the entire parsed YAML structure1, your config struct, or all the variables you have set from environment variables. No matter how you load your configuration, log it (but mask your secrets).

item.title: Salt vs. Ansible
item.description:
Some time ago was set to evaluate configuration management systems. I’ve heard opinions from someone I respect that Puppet and Chef were complicated beasts to get up and running, and since I am a Python guy I’ve generally always kept an eye on Ansible and Salt. Ruby is so far not my thing, but hey let’s not start a flamewar about that!

Last year I got to spend a good 6 months working with Ansible for provisioning of servers. I became very familiar with the tool. In that project, Ansible was mostly chosen because it was easy to get started and had good documentation. The team I was working with was especially fond of the Best Practises documentation which got us started quickly and taught us what structure had worked previously.
